rows.title: Policy
rows.read: Almost every major central bank still leans toward raising rates because high oil keeps inflation up. A stock-market scare has trimmed bets on a December Federal Reserve hike, which takes a little support from the dollar. Switzerland remains the odd one out.
rows.figure: Fed Oct 28 hold ~93%, Dec hike ~85% (from ~90%); BoC Oct 28 hike ~80–87%; RBNZ Oct 28 ~98%; BoE Nov 5 ~90–95%, Dec ~48–61%; RBA Nov 3 ~44–50%; ECB Dec ~88%; BoJ Dec ~80%

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: Households are starting to pull back where energy bills bite hardest. UK shoppers spent less and their confidence slumped, and Australia's private sector shrank. Weaker growth makes it harder for those central banks to keep raising rates.
rows.figure: UK retail sales Sep −0.4% m/m (−0.1% fc); GfK Oct −24 (−14 fc); Australia flash composite PMI 47.7 (51.3 prior); Japan flash PMI 52.3 (factories 53.3, services 52.0)

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Energy keeps inflation high almost everywhere, which is why so many central banks lean toward hikes. Japan's inflation is back above the Bank of Japan's goal and spreading beyond fuel, which strengthens the case for a December hike there and helps the yen.
rows.figure: Japan core CPI Sep 2.1% y/y (2.1% fc), ex-food and energy 2.4%; UK CPI Sep 3.5%; Canada factory-gate prices +2.0% m/m; Australia input costs fastest since May

rows.title: Risk
rows.read: Investors are nervous: worries about AI spending keep hitting tech shares, and attacks on Saudi Arabia add to the unease. Money is going into US government bonds and the yen, while gold keeps sliding instead of acting as a shelter.
rows.figure: Nikkei −1.3% Fri; US 10Y ~4.96%; USD/JPY low ~156.3, yen strongest in over a month; gold ~$4,020, two-month low

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.read: Oil is near its highest since May as Houthi attacks reach deeper into Saudi Arabia and Libyan output dips. That helps exporters like Canada and hurts big energy importers like Japan and the euro area.
rows.figure: Brent ~$114 (third weekly gain in sight); US crude ~$100; Aramco Dhahran HQ evacuated; Libya pipeline shut

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar, even as a Bank of Canada hike looks likely, which leaves those bets exposed if the loonie keeps rising. They also bet against the kiwi and the euro. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 13: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against EUR and NZD (added), for AUD (trimmed; real money strongly against), against JPY (real money for), strongly for gold (trimmed); next report Fri Oct 23

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.read: Government finances are weighing on the euro: France pays more than 5% to borrow for ten years, near its widest gap over Germany since 2011. Moody's reviews France's rating tonight, and Britain's budget follows on October 28, with shoppers already holding back ahead of it.
rows.figure: France 10Y above 5%; OAT–Bund near widest since 2011; Moody's on France Fri Oct 23 (after European close); French revenue vote Oct 27; UK budget Oct 28
